## Why This Is Asked
Tests a practical, low‑complexity policy enforcement pattern in CNFs: per-tenant configuration, header-based routing, and end-to-end validation.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace ConfigMaps for per-tenant config
- Sidecar‑driven request filtering using tenantID and path prefixes
- 403 responses with centralized logging for audit

## Code Example
```text
# Pseudo-logic
tenant = req.headers['X-TENANT-ID']
prefixes = cnf.denylist[tenant] or []
for p in prefixes:
  if req.path.startswith(p):
    return 403
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Distributed tracing fundamentals and W3C Trace Context
- Tenant-scoped attributes and resource naming conventions

- Sampling strategies and their impact on observability versus cost

## Code Example

```yaml
# OpenTelemetry Collector config (minimal)
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo:4317
    headers:
      x-tenant-id: "${TENANT_ID}"
processors:
  resource:
    attributes:
      - key: tenant_id
        value: "${TENANT_ID}"
        action: upsert
  batch: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Namespace ConfigMap per-tenant feature flags
- Sidecar-based request rewriting for canary paths

- Safe defaults when feature flag is off

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap example
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.canary
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  enabled: "true"
  target: "/v1/foo"
```
```yaml
# Sidecar snippet (pseudo)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-sidecar
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: sidecar
        image: cnf/sidecar:latest
        env:
        - name: CANARY_ENABLED
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.canary

        - name: CANARY_TARGET
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.canary
              key: target
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy-as-code proficiency, practical use of Gatekeeper/OPA, and ability to derive concrete manifests and validation steps for a CNF multi-tenant setup.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- ReadOnlyRootFilesystem, hostNetwork, and Privileged security controls
- Namespace-scoped policy targeting CNFs
- Lightweight test manifests to validate allow/deny paths

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfnamespacesecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
        listKind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraintList
        plural: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraints
        singular: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraint
  targets:
  - target: admissionreviews
    rego: |
      package cnfnamespacesecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.hostNetwork
        msg := "hostNetwork is forbidden for CNFs"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers
        # fallback for non-pods
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
        msg := "readOnlyRootFilesystem is required for all containers"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.privileged == true
        msg := "privileged containers are disallowed"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: cnfnamespacesecurity.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: cnf-a-security
spec:
  namespace: cnf-a
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-cnf
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      privileged: false
      runAsNonRoot: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# Non-compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-cnf
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
      privileged: true
```

## Follow-up Steps

- Apply ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, and test manifests in a single namespace and observe denial events for non-compliant pods.
- Extend with a quick kubectl patch to simulate remediation and re-validate.

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates understanding of tenant isolation, mTLS, and certificate rotation using cert-manager in a CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway context. It also assesses practical knowledge of in-cluster secret management and sidecar integration patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Secrets and per-tenant namespace isolation
- Mutual TLS termination in a gateway sidecar
- cert-manager Issuers and automatic certificate rotation
- Tenant identity extraction from X.509 certificates

## Code Example
```yaml
# Per-tenant CA Issuer
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca-cert
---
# Certificate with auto-rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-server-tls
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  secretName: tenant-<id>-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  duration: 168h
  renewBefore: 72h
  dnsNames:
    - gateway.tenant-namespace.svc.cluster.local
  subject:
    organizations:
      - tenant-<id>
---
# Gateway Deployment with mTLS sidecar
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      - name: mtls-sidecar
        image: mtls-proxy:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 9443
        env:
        - name: TENANT_CA_PATH
          value: /etc/certs/ca.crt
        - name: VALIDATE_CLIENT_CERTS
          value: "true"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
        - name: tenant-ca
          mountPath: /etc/certs
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tenant-<id>-tls
      - name: tenant-ca
        secret:
          secretName: tenant-ca-cert
```

## Validation One-Namespace Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-001
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-cert
  namespace: tenant-001
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-encoded-ca-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-encoded-ca-key>
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: tenant-001
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca-cert
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-001-tls
  namespace: tenant-001
spec:
  secretName: tenant-001-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  duration: 168h
  renewBefore: 72h
  dnsNames:
    - gateway.tenant-001.svc.cluster.local
  subject:
    organizations:
      - tenant-001
```

## Key Implementation Details
1. **Certificate Rotation**: cert-manager automatically renews certificates before expiration using the `renewBefore` field
2. **Tenant Isolation**: Each tenant has isolated namespaces, CAs, and TLS secrets
3. **mTLS Validation**: The sidecar validates client certificates against the tenant-specific CA
4. **Tenant ID Extraction**: The tenant ID is extracted from the certificate subject (organization field) to enforce access policies

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates candidate understanding of tenant-scoped dynamic capability negotiation and caching in cloud-native environments, ensuring isolation and correctness at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Tenant-scoped capability registry (implemented as a CRD or ConfigMap)
- Per-tenant, TTL-based cache in the sidecar for performance optimization
- Highest common version selection using semantic versioning
- HTTP 406 Not Acceptable response when no compatible version exists; graceful default fallback
- Observability: Prometheus metrics, structured logging, and distributed tracing

## Code Example

```go
// Pseudocode for version negotiation
func negotiate(upstreamVersions []string, tenantID string) string {
    tenantVersions := registry.GetVersions(tenantID)
    allowed := intersect(upstreamVersions, tenantVersions)
    if len(allowed) == 0 {
        return DEFAULT_VERSION
    }
    return highestVersion(allowed)
}
```

## Implementation Highlights

- Extract X-TENANT-ID header in sidecar middleware
- Query central registry for tenant capabilities
- Compute intersection with upstream supported versions
- Select highest compatible version using semver comparison
- Store result in tenant-scoped cache with configurable TTL
- Return 406 if negotiation fails and no default is configured

Tests cross-cluster authorization reasoning and practical application of SPIFFE, OPA, and revocation in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE IDs and SPIRE binding
- OPA/rego policies for tenant, path, verb

## Code Example
```rego
package cnf.auth

default allow = false

allow {
  input.tenant_id == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].id
  input.spiffe_id == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].spiffe
  input.verb == "GET"
  startswith(input.path, data.tenants[input.tenant_id].path)
}
```
